title: Climate Funding for Poorer Nations Stalls as Needs Grow
subtitle: A new UN report warns that financial support for climate adaptation is falling behind the rising costs of extreme weather.

summary.en: A new United Nations report shows that money to help developing countries deal with climate change has stopped growing. Wealthy nations are not meeting their promises to provide enough financial support for adaptation. Developing countries need billions of dollars to protect themselves from floods, heatwaves, and rising sea levels. Many poor nations are suffering the most despite contributing the least to global warming. Experts warn that failing to act now will make future costs much higher and put millions of people at risk.
summary.zh: 一份新的聯合國報告顯示，協助開發中國家應對氣候變遷的資金已停止成長。富裕國家未能履行提供足夠調適財務援助的承諾。開發中國家需要數十億美元來保護自身免受洪水、熱浪與海平面上升的威脅。許多貧窮國家儘管對全球暖化的貢獻最少，卻承受著最嚴重的苦果。專家警告，若現在不採取行動，未來的成本將會高出許多，並使數百萬人陷入險境。

paragraphs.en: The world is facing a growing problem as the climate crisis gets worse. According to The Guardian Environment, money meant to help poorer countries deal with the effects of global heating has stopped increasing. Since 2022, financial support has remained flat or even dropped. This is happening at the same time that scientists warn that global temperatures are rising faster than expected, leading to more extreme weather events.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著氣候危機日益惡化，全球正面臨越來越嚴峻的問題。根據《衛報環境版》（The Guardian Environment）報導，旨在協助貧窮國家應對全球暖化影響的資金已停止成長。自二〇二二年以來，財務援助金額停滯不前，甚至出現下滑。與此同時，科學家警告全球氣溫上升的速度超出預期，導致極端天氣事件頻發。

paragraphs.en: Adaptation refers to the actions countries take to protect themselves from climate change. This includes building stronger infrastructure, such as sea walls to stop flooding, creating early warning systems for storms, and finding ways to grow food during long droughts. The United Nations Environment Programme reports that 155 developing nations will need $305 billion every year by 2035 to handle these challenges. These countries are dealing with more intense heatwaves, fires, and rising sea levels caused by decades of burning fossil fuels, mostly in wealthy nations.
paragraphs.zh: 「調適」是指各國為保護自身免受氣候變遷影響所採取的行動。這包括建立更堅固的基礎設施，例如防止洪水的海堤、建立風暴預警系統，以及尋找在長期乾旱期間種植糧食的方法。聯合國環境規劃署（United Nations Environment Programme）指出，到二〇三五年，一百五十五個開發中國家每年將需要三千零五十億美元來應對這些挑戰。這些國家正承受著由富裕國家數十年來燃燒化石燃料所引發的更強烈熱浪、火災及海平面上升之苦。

paragraphs.en: However, the reality is far from what is needed. The Guardian Environment reports that in 2024, financial support from rich to poor countries reached only $32 billion. This was only a small increase from the previous year and actually lower than the peak seen in 2022. One reason for this decline is that many European governments are now spending more of their budgets on defense, or military spending, rather than climate aid. This current level of funding is far behind the goal of reaching $40 billion by 2025.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，現實情況與需求相去甚遠。《衛報環境版》報導，二〇二四年富裕國家提供給貧窮國家的財務援助僅達三百二十億美元。這與前一年相比僅有微幅成長，且實際上低於二〇二二年的高峰。造成此一衰退的原因之一，是許多歐洲政府目前將更多預算用於國防或軍事支出，而非氣候援助。目前的資金水準距離二〇二五年達到四百億美元的目標仍有很大差距。

paragraphs.en: Some of the most vulnerable nations are being hit the hardest. Small island states and the world’s least developed countries are suffering the most from climate change, yet they have the least money to pay for protection. The UN estimates that these countries need between $40 billion and $50 billion each year. Even though they have the greatest need, these nations actually received 16% less financial support in 2024 than they did two years earlier. This means they are struggling to build the necessary tools, like firefighting equipment and better flood defenses, to keep their people safe.
paragraphs.zh: 一些最脆弱的國家正遭受最嚴重的衝擊。小型島國與全球最不發達國家受氣候變遷之苦最深，卻擁有最少的資金來支付防護費用。聯合國估計，這些國家每年需要四百億至五百億美元。儘管需求最大，這些國家在二〇二四年實際獲得的財務援助卻比兩年前減少了百分之十六。這意味著他們難以建立必要的工具，例如消防設備與更好的防洪設施，以保障人民的安全。

paragraphs.en: Between 2020 and 2025, low- and middle-income countries were home to 99% of the 765 million people affected by floods and landslides. Many of these countries lack the technology to monitor how many people die from heat or how much damage happens to their environment. Because of this, the true scale of the crisis is likely even worse than what is currently reported. A new fund created to help with "loss and damage"—which refers to the costs of climate impacts that cannot be avoided or fixed—is already struggling. In its first round of requests, 119 developing countries asked for $2.8 billion, but only $342 million was available.
paragraphs.zh: 在二〇二〇年至二〇二五年期間，全球有七億六千五百萬人受到洪水與土石流影響，其中百分之九十九居住在低收入與中等收入國家。許多國家缺乏監測技術，無法統計有多少人死於高溫，或環境受到多大程度的破壞。因此，危機的真實規模很可能比目前報導的還要嚴重。一項為協助「損失與損害」（指無法避免或修復的氣候影響成本）而設立的新基金已陷入困境。在首輪申請中，一百一十九個開發中國家請求二十八億美元，但實際可用的資金僅有三億四千兩百萬美元。

paragraphs.en: Inger Andersen, the executive director of the UN Environment Programme, explained that a rise in global temperatures is now unavoidable. This makes climate impacts more frequent and harder to predict. She noted that for countries that have contributed the least to the problem but suffer the most, this is a difficult reality. She described adaptation finance as a vital investment in global safety. By protecting frontline communities, the world can prevent forced movement of people and keep food supplies secure.
paragraphs.zh: 聯合國環境規劃署執行主任安德森（Inger Andersen）解釋說，全球氣溫上升已不可避免，這使得氣候影響變得更加頻繁且難以預測。她指出，對於那些對氣候問題貢獻最少卻受害最深的國家而言，這是一個艱難的現實。她將調適資金形容為對全球安全至關重要的投資。透過保護處於第一線的社區，全球可以防止人口被迫遷移，並確保糧食供應穩定。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, there is some hope for improvement. At the Cop30 climate talks held in Brazil last year, wealthy nations promised to triple the amount of money they provide for adaptation by 2035. If they reach this goal, the total could be between $85 billion and $120 billion. While this would help reduce the current gap, the UN report notes that it would still only cover about 20% to 29% of what is actually needed. Experts warn that delays in providing this money do not just increase the long-term costs; they also make it much harder for these countries to cope with the dangers they face today.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，仍有一絲改善的希望。在去年於巴西舉行的聯合國氣候變遷大會（Cop30）上，富裕國家承諾到二〇三五年將其提供的調適資金增加至三倍。若能達成此目標，總額將可達八百五十億至一千兩百億美元。雖然這有助於縮小目前的缺口，但聯合國報告指出，這仍僅能涵蓋實際需求量的百分之二十至二十九。專家警告，提供資金的延宕不僅會增加長期成本，更會讓這些國家難以應對當前所面臨的危險。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Not changing or increasing; remaining at the same level.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（平坦的），這裡用來形容財務數據沒有增長。文中：Since 2022, financial support has remained flat or even dropped.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Most directly affected by a problem or situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 處於第一線的、最直接受影響的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（前線），這裡作形容詞修飾社區，指最先遭受氣候變遷衝擊的群體。文中：By protecting frontline communities, the world can prevent forced movement of people and keep food supplies secure.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A difference between two things, often between what is needed and what is actually available.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（縫隙），這裡指實際需求與資金供給之間的落差。文中：While this would help reduce the current gap, the UN report notes that it would still only cover about 20% to 29% of what is actually needed.

sources.name: The Guardian Environment
sources.title: Funding to help poorer countries cope with climate crisis has stalled, says UN

quiz.question: According to the article, what is one major reason why financial support for climate adaptation has declined since 2022?

options.A: Developing nations have requested less money than in previous years.
options.B: Many European governments are prioritizing military and defense spending.
options.C: The United Nations has officially lowered the annual funding goal to $32 billion.
options.D: Wealthy nations have successfully met their 2025 climate aid targets early.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，作者明確指出資金下降的原因之一是許多歐洲政府將預算轉向國防或軍事支出。選項 A 錯誤，因為發展中國家需求依然巨大；選項 C 錯誤，因為 320 億美元是實際撥款金額，而非目標；選項 D 錯誤，因為文章提到目前的資金遠落後於 2025 年的目標。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the 'loss and damage' fund mentioned in the fifth paragraph?

options.A: It is sufficient to cover the costs of all climate-related disasters.
options.B: It is primarily used to build new sea walls and infrastructure.
options.C: The demand for financial assistance far exceeds the current supply of funds.
options.D: It was created specifically to help wealthy nations recover from heatwaves.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第五段提到 119 個發展中國家請求 28 億美元，但僅有 3.42 億美元可用，這顯示供需嚴重失衡。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 B 錯誤，因為該基金處理的是「無法避免或修復」的損害，而非預防性的基礎建設；選項 D 錯誤，因為該基金是為了幫助發展中國家，而非富裕國家。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the author mean by describing adaptation finance as a 'vital investment'?

options.A: It is an essential action that provides long-term benefits for global security.
options.B: It is a profitable business venture that generates money for wealthy countries.
options.C: It is a temporary solution that will soon be replaced by private funding.
options.D: It is a risky financial gamble that may not produce any positive results.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境下，「vital investment」指的是為了全球安全而投入的必要資源，能預防被迫遷徙並確保糧食供應。選項 B 將「investment」誤解為商業獲利；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章強調這是長期需求；選項 D 錯誤，因為作者將其視為保護社區的安全措施，而非投機行為。

quiz.question: What is the central argument of this article regarding climate adaptation finance?

options.A: The climate crisis is improving because wealthy nations have tripled their aid.
options.B: Developing nations should rely on their own technology to solve climate issues.
options.C: There is a significant gap between the urgent needs of vulnerable nations and the actual financial support provided.
options.D: The UN is solely responsible for the lack of progress in global climate funding.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於強調氣候危機加劇，但富裕國家提供的資金遠遠不足以應對發展中國家的需求，導致嚴重的資金缺口。選項 A 與事實不符；選項 B 文章並未提倡；選項 D 錯誤，文章並未將責任全歸咎於聯合國，而是指出富裕國家預算分配與承諾落實的問題。
